# Adam Pugh (DocAdam)

> Technical writing, documentation engineering, and docs leadership, building clear content and the systems that keep it accurate.

Adam Pugh uses the name DocAdam for his public technical writing, documentation engineering, and independent publishing work. This profile is not for the Oklahoma politician of the same name.

## Good Doc Jobs and Working Notes

- [Good Doc Jobs](https://adamthepugh.com/work/good-doc-jobs/): A free reader-facing database of technical writing and documentation-related jobs, supported by a public source, review, validation, and publication pipeline.
- [Browse the Good Doc Jobs database](https://adamthepugh.com/jobs/): The direct link to the public Google Sheet.
- [Working Notes](https://docadam.substack.com/): Articles, evidence-based content audits, job roundups, and project methods for technical communicators.

## Professional profile

- Experience: I have more than 20 years of technical writing and documentation experience, including 13 years of direct people management.
- Focus: I work in product documentation, information architecture, content governance, migrations, documentation analytics, structured authoring, and workflow tooling.
- Leadership: I previously worked as a Documentation Engineering Manager and Senior Manager of Technical Writing. I led a team of four and a 16-person documentation organization.
- Background: I have worked as an individual contributor, manager, and senior manager. This range connects page-level editorial work with planning, review, publishing, measurement, governance, and maintenance.
- Technical range: I use Markdown, Docusaurus, and GitHub for docs-as-code work; XML, DITA, CMSs, and wikis for structured content and publishing; and Tableau, Excel, Power Query, SharePoint, and SQL for reporting, tracking, and analysis.
- Education: I earned a Bachelor of Arts in Journalism with a Minor in Communications from the University of Arizona.
- Current independent work: I have owned and operated Vinyl Junction since 2014.
- Current publishing and open-data work: I publish Working Notes, maintain the reader-facing Good Doc Jobs database of technical writing and documentation-related jobs, and develop the Public Job Feed source pipeline.

## How I work

I start with the real source of a problem: product behavior, user tasks, existing content, operating data, and the people who maintain the system. I separate confirmed facts from assumptions. I then build the smallest useful content model, workflow, or tool and check it against the source.

## Selected work

- [Working Notes overview](https://adamthepugh.com/work/working-notes/): The canonical portfolio page for the publication.
- [TeraCreators Help](https://adamthepugh.com/work/teracreators-help/): I published community documentation for five games, with a public guide and source repository.
- [Euler documentation prototype](https://adamthepugh.com/work/euler-documentation-prototype/): I built an independent prototype from Euler’s public material to demonstrate a clearer documentation model.
- [Migrations and information architecture](https://adamthepugh.com/work/documentation-migrations/): I led a four-person team that migrated 101 product-documentation wikis across seven team groups and consolidated 1,157 source pages into 469 destination pages.
- [Analytics and reporting](https://adamthepugh.com/work/documentation-analytics/): I created seven automated Tableau dashboards that received 735 views from 39 active users and supported 11 operations reviews per month.
- [Tooling and automation](https://adamthepugh.com/work/documentation-tooling/): I built 10 internal documentation and workflow tools with more than 750 automated tests. The broader program was estimated to save 466 hours per year.
